title: Heroin Addiction Treatment in New York and NYSHIP
desc: Understand heroin addiction, evidence-based treatment options like MAT, and how NYSHIP/Empire Plan may cover detox and rehab for New York State employees.
h1: Heroin Addiction Treatment in New York: What NYSHIP Members Should Know
author: NYSHIP Detox Editorial Team
bodyHtml:
Heroin use disorder is a serious, chronic medical condition—and it is treatable. For New York State employees and their dependents enrolled in NYSHIP (the New York State Health Insurance Program), including the Empire Plan, understanding what treatment options exist and how coverage may apply is an important first step toward recovery. This article is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice; please consult a qualified healthcare provider for guidance specific to your situation.

How Heroin Addiction Develops

Heroin is a rapidly acting opioid derived from morphine. According to the National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA), heroin binds to opioid receptors in the brain with high affinity, producing an intense but short-lived euphoria followed by drowsiness. Repeated use causes the brain to adapt: tolerance develops, and physical dependence follows. Heroin use disorder can develop quickly, making early intervention critical.

Evidence-Based Medications for Heroin Use Disorder

Medication-assisted treatment (MAT) is the gold-standard, evidence-based approach for opioid use disorder. Three FDA-approved medications are available:

  • Buprenorphine (Suboxone, Subutex): A partial opioid agonist that reduces cravings and withdrawal without producing the same euphoric effect as heroin.
  • Methadone: A long-acting full opioid agonist dispensed through federally regulated opioid treatment programs.
  • Naltrexone (Vivitrol): An opioid antagonist that blocks the effects of opioids entirely.

According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), MAT reduces opioid use, decreases overdose deaths, and improves social functioning.

NYSHIP and Empire Plan Coverage

NYSHIP members enrolled in the Empire Plan or other participating plans may have benefits that apply to medically necessary substance use disorder treatment, including detoxification, inpatient rehabilitation, and outpatient services. Under the federal Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA), insurance plans cannot impose more restrictive limits on SUD treatment than on comparable medical care. Call the SAMHSA National Helpline at 1-800-662-4357 (free, confidential, 24/7) or contact us at 213-321-6518 for a free benefits verification.

If you or a loved one is in crisis, call or text the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This content is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice.

sources.name: CDC: Medications for Opioid Use Disorder
NIDA: Medications to Treat Opioid Use Disorder

faq.q: Does NYSHIP cover heroin detox and rehab?
faq.a: NYSHIP/Empire Plan members may have benefits for medically necessary substance use disorder treatment, including detox and inpatient or outpatient rehab. Coverage specifics vary by plan. Call 213-321-6518 to verify.

faq.q: Will my employer know if I seek treatment for heroin addiction?
faq.a: No. Federal law (42 CFR Part 2) protects substance use disorder treatment records with stricter confidentiality rules than standard HIPAA.

faq.q: What is medication-assisted treatment and is it effective for heroin?
faq.a: MAT combines FDA-approved medications with counseling and support services. According to NIDA and the CDC, MAT significantly reduces illicit opioid use, lowers overdose mortality, and improves long-term recovery outcomes.

faq.q: What should I do if someone is overdosing on heroin?
faq.a: Call 911 immediately. If naloxone (Narcan) is available, administer it right away. New York's Good Samaritan Law protects people who call 911 in good faith during an overdose.

title: Employee Assistance Programs and Addiction Help
desc: NY State employees can use their Employee Assistance Program alongside NYSHIP coverage to access confidential addiction assessment, referrals, and treatment support.
h1: Employee Assistance Programs and Addiction Treatment for NY State Employees
author: NYSHIP Detox Editorial Team
bodyHtml:
New York State and government employees have access to a layered set of supports when dealing with addiction. One that is often overlooked is the Employee Assistance Program (EAP). Understanding how EAPs work, and how they fit alongside NYSHIP insurance benefits, can make a real difference in getting help quickly. This article is general education, not medical or legal advice; confirm the details of your specific program with your HR office or EAP provider.

What Is an Employee Assistance Program?

An EAP is a confidential, employer-sponsored benefit that provides assessment, short-term counseling, and referrals for personal and work-related concerns, including substance use and mental health issues. According to the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA), EAPs are an important pathway to connecting workers with appropriate care.

How EAP and NYSHIP Work Together

The most effective use of these benefits is usually sequential: contact the EAP first for a confidential assessment and referral, then use your NYSHIP benefits to cover the cost of actual treatment. The National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA) describes addiction as a treatable, chronic medical condition. Getting a professional assessment is an important first step.

Confidentiality Protections

EAP records are kept separate from your employment record. The SAMHSA confidentiality guidance explains that substance use treatment records held by federally assisted programs prevent disclosure to an employer without your explicit written consent.

Getting Started

You can typically reach your EAP by calling the toll-free number listed in your benefits materials. For immediate questions about treatment, our team is available at 213-321-6518. For free, confidential, 24/7 treatment referrals, call the SAMHSA National Helpline at 1-800-662-4357. If you are in crisis, call or text the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. This content is for educational purposes only.

sources.name: NIDA — Understanding Drug Use and Addiction

faq.q: Can my supervisor find out I contacted the EAP about addiction?
faq.a: No. EAP records are separate from employment records, and counselors operate under strict confidentiality rules.

faq.q: Does my EAP cover the cost of addiction treatment?
faq.a: EAPs typically provide assessment, short-term counseling, and referrals at no cost, but they are not a source of insurance coverage for treatment. Medically necessary care is generally covered through your NYSHIP or Empire Plan benefits.

faq.q: How do I contact the EAP as a NY State employee?
faq.a: Most NY State employees can reach the EAP through the toll-free number listed in their benefits materials or by contacting their HR office. Our team can also help at 213-321-6518.

faq.q: Can the EAP help if I am worried about a family member's addiction?
faq.a: Many EAPs extend services to dependents and family members as well as employees.

title: Mindfulness-Based Relapse Prevention: A NYSHIP Guide
desc: Mindfulness-based relapse prevention (MBRP) builds craving awareness and reduces relapse risk. Evidence-based guidance for NYSHIP members in recovery.
h1: Mindfulness-Based Relapse Prevention: Evidence and Practice for NY State Employees
author: NYSHIP Detox Editorial Team
bodyHtml:
Recovery from addiction is not a single event but an ongoing process — and one of the most practical sets of tools developed to support long-term sobriety draws on mindfulness. Mindfulness-Based Relapse Prevention (MBRP) is a structured, evidence-based program that teaches people in recovery to recognize and respond to high-risk situations, cravings, and emotional triggers with awareness rather than automatic reaction. This article is general education, not medical or clinical advice. If you or a loved one is in crisis, call or text 988, or reach the SAMHSA National Helpline at 1-800-662-4357.

What Is Mindfulness-Based Relapse Prevention?

MBRP was developed by researchers at the University of Washington as an integration of mindfulness meditation practices with cognitive-behavioral relapse prevention strategies. According to the National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA), effective addiction treatment must address not just the physical aspects of dependence but also the behavioral and psychological patterns that sustain substance use.

The Evidence Base for MBRP

The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) recognizes mindfulness-based approaches as evidence-supported practices for both substance use disorders and co-occurring mental health conditions. The National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA) likewise recognizes that behavioral approaches are a cornerstone of effective treatment.

How MBRP Fits Into NYSHIP-Covered Care

For NY State employees accessing treatment through NYSHIP rehab benefits, MBRP typically appears as a component of intensive outpatient (IOP) programming or as a structured aftercare intervention. According to MedlinePlus, substance use disorders are chronic conditions that benefit from long-term support. Call 213-321-6518 for a free, confidential conversation about your treatment options and NYSHIP coverage. For free, 24/7 treatment support, call the SAMHSA National Helpline at 1-800-662-4357. If you or a loved one is in crisis, call or text 988.

sources.name: NIAAA — Treatment for Alcohol Problems: Finding and Getting Help

faq.q: Is mindfulness-based relapse prevention covered by NYSHIP?
faq.a: Evidence-based behavioral therapies for addiction treatment, including MBRP-informed approaches, are generally covered by NYSHIP and the Empire Plan when clinically indicated, under federal mental health parity protections. Call 213-321-6518 for a free benefits verification.

faq.q: Do I need meditation experience to participate in MBRP?
faq.a: No. MBRP is designed to be learned from the ground up — no prior meditation experience is required or expected.

faq.q: How long does a standard MBRP program take?
faq.a: A standard MBRP curriculum consists of eight weekly group sessions, each typically lasting about two hours.

faq.q: Can MBRP help with anxiety and depression in recovery?
faq.a: MBRP is specifically designed to address emotional discomfort — including anxiety, low mood, and stress — that commonly drives relapse risk. It is a complement to, not a replacement for, clinical treatment.

title: Benzodiazepine Withdrawal: A Guide for NYSHIP Members
desc: Why benzodiazepine withdrawal can be life-threatening, how medically supervised detox helps, and how NYSHIP and the Empire Plan may cover care for NY State employees.
h1: Benzodiazepine Withdrawal: A Guide for NYSHIP Members
author: NYSHIP Detox Editorial Team
bodyHtml:
Benzodiazepines — medications such as Xanax (alprazolam), Valium (diazepam), Klonopin (clonazepam), and Ativan (lorazepam) — are among the most commonly prescribed drugs in the United States. They are prescribed for anxiety, panic disorder, insomnia, and seizures, and many New York State and government employees have received them through legitimate prescriptions. What is less commonly understood is that benzodiazepines can cause physical dependence even when taken as prescribed — and that stopping them abruptly can be medically dangerous. This article is for educational purposes only and is not medical advice.

How Benzodiazepine Dependence Develops

Benzodiazepines work by enhancing the calming effects of a brain chemical called GABA (gamma-aminobutyric acid), reducing anxiety and promoting sleep. With regular use over weeks or months, the brain adapts to their presence by reducing its own GABA activity. When the medication is then reduced or stopped suddenly, the nervous system can become dangerously overactivated. According to MedlinePlus, a service of the National Library of Medicine, dependence can develop even in people who take these medications exactly as prescribed — which is why doctors typically advise gradual tapering rather than sudden discontinuation.

Why Benzodiazepine Withdrawal Can Be Life-Threatening

Severe benzodiazepine withdrawal is a medical emergency. Unlike opioid withdrawal — which is very uncomfortable but rarely directly fatal — withdrawal from benzodiazepines shares a dangerous mechanism with alcohol withdrawal: both can cause grand mal seizures and a condition called delirium tremens, involving severe confusion, agitation, fever, and hallucinations. The National Institute on Drug Abuse (NIDA) identifies benzodiazepines as one of the prescription drug classes associated with the highest risk of dangerous withdrawal. Do not stop benzodiazepines abruptly or without medical guidance. The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) strongly recommends professionally supervised withdrawal management for this class of medication.

What Medically Supervised Benzodiazepine Detox Looks Like

The safest approach to stopping benzodiazepines is a medically supervised gradual taper — a structured, slow reduction of the dose that allows the brain and nervous system to readjust without triggering dangerous rebound activity. In a supervised detox setting, a clinical team:

  • Assesses your current dose, duration of use, and overall medical history
  • Designs an individualized taper schedule
  • Monitors vital signs and neurological status around the clock
  • Provides medications to prevent complications, including seizures
  • Offers emotional support and prepares you for the next phase of care

Benzodiazepine withdrawal can be prolonged — lasting weeks or months in some cases — which is why continuous medical supervision throughout the taper is important. The National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA), whose guidance on alcohol withdrawal shares key clinical principles with benzodiazepine management, emphasizes that supervised care reduces life-threatening complications that self-managed withdrawal cannot address.

NYSHIP and Empire Plan Coverage for Benzodiazepine Detox

For New York State and government employees enrolled in NYSHIP — including the Empire Plan and NYSHIP-participating HMOs — medically necessary substance use disorder treatment is generally a covered benefit. Under the federal Mental Health Parity and Addiction Equity Act (MHPAEA), plans that cover mental health and substance use treatment cannot apply more restrictive terms than they apply to comparable medical benefits. Benzodiazepine dependence is a recognized medical condition, and inpatient or residential detox is typically covered when a clinical assessment determines it is medically necessary.

Coverage specifics — including applicable copays, deductibles, prior authorization requirements, and network rules — vary by plan. Visit our NYSHIP rehab coverage page or call us at 213-321-6518 for a free, confidential benefits verification.

Confidentiality Protections for NY State Employees

A common concern for government employees is whether seeking treatment could affect their employment. Federal law provides strong protections. Substance use disorder treatment records are protected by 42 CFR Part 2, which imposes stricter confidentiality requirements than standard HIPAA — your employer cannot access your treatment records without your explicit written consent. Eligible employees may also be entitled to up to 12 weeks of job-protected leave under the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA) for treatment of a serious health condition. These are general legal outlines; confirm specifics with your HR office or a qualified attorney.

Treating the Underlying Condition After Detox

Because benzodiazepines are frequently prescribed for anxiety, panic disorder, or insomnia, successful long-term recovery also means addressing those underlying conditions. According to MedlinePlus, anxiety disorders are highly treatable through evidence-based approaches such as cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) and, where appropriate, non-addictive medications. An integrated approach that treats both the dependence and the original condition gives recovery a much more durable foundation. You can read more on our NYSHIP coverage verification page about how ongoing behavioral health care is typically covered.

Getting Help

If you or a loved one is dependent on benzodiazepines, please do not try to stop alone. For free, confidential, 24/7 treatment referrals, call the SAMHSA National Helpline at 1-800-662-4357. If you or someone you know is in crisis or having thoughts of suicide, call or text the 988 Suicide and Crisis Lifeline. For questions about using NYSHIP or Empire Plan coverage for benzodiazepine detox, call us at 213-321-6518. This content is for educational purposes only and does not constitute medical or legal advice.

sources.name: NIAAA — Treatment for Alcohol Problems: Finding and Getting Help

faq.q: Can benzodiazepine withdrawal really be dangerous?
faq.a: Yes. Unlike opioid withdrawal, benzodiazepine withdrawal can cause grand mal seizures and delirium tremens, which can be life-threatening — similar to severe alcohol withdrawal. Never stop benzodiazepines abruptly without medical guidance.

NYSHIP and the Empire Plan typically cover medically necessary substance use disorder treatment, including supervised detox. Under federal parity law, coverage must be comparable to medical benefits. Details vary by plan. Call 213-321-6518 for a free, confidential benefits verification.

faq.q: Will my employer find out if I seek treatment for benzodiazepine dependence?
faq.a: No. Federal law (42 CFR Part 2) protects substance use disorder treatment records with stricter confidentiality than standard HIPAA. Your employer cannot access your treatment records without your explicit written consent.

faq.q: How long does benzodiazepine detox take?
faq.a: Unlike opioid detox, benzodiazepine withdrawal typically requires a gradual taper lasting weeks to months, depending on the specific medication, dose, and duration of use. Medical supervision throughout is important because complications can develop at any stage.
